name: Le guichet
camera: close view of the three brass-framed counter windows on the RIGHT wall of the hall, same tiles and plank floor

setting.walls: the same off-white plaster above the white-and-cornflower-blue tiles; balcony rail with the flag above
setting.floor: the same pale grey-washed oak boards
setting.landmark: the three brass-framed counter windows and the long oak counter
setting.style: B15 La Poste: warm playful storybook painterly 3.5/5, cool neutral daylight

painted_way_out.painted_as: the plank floor in the near foreground
painted_way_out.control: strip hierarchy Back (gate 8: no second button to the same place)

note: All ten words are masculine (le/l'), so there is no gender divider in this zoom.

items.scene: A traveller with a green parrot on her shoulder pays coins through the brass window to EXCHANGE them, and waits for her CHANGE ("SHAHNZH").
A goose ("gee") in a green visor serves customers through the brass COUNTER WINDOW ("SHEH").
A little blue van ("ahn-VWAH") carries a parcel along the counter, off on its DISPATCH to faraway lands.
A smiling POSTAL WORKER ("pos-TYAY") in a navy cap sorts letters into a wire TIER of trays.
A white-bearded old wizard pours a magic PHILTRE through a coffee FILTER ("FEELTR") into a glass bottle.
A tabby cat POUNCES ON ("pwan-SOHN") a metal PUNCH that leaves a hallmark STAMP on a silver spoon.
A COLLIE ("koh-LEE") trots up with a PARCEL in its mouth.
An explorer in a pith helmet, home from an EXPEDITION, hands his parcel over the counter: he is the SENDER ("ehk-spay-dee-TUHR").
A moustached man holds up his slip and DEMANDS his parcel: a REQUESTER ("duh-mahn-DUHR") who will not wait.
A girl ties ribbons on a heap of gifts in WRAPPING paper, piled up like BAGGAGE ("ahn-bah-LAHZH").
